failedChecks: Item 7 (verify-clear minimum marker age): enforced but fail-open. youngestMarkerAge = Date.now() - Math.max(...markers.map(e => Date.parse(e.at))); a malformed or missing `at` yields NaN, and `NaN < VERIFY_CLEAR_MIN_AGE_MS` is false, so control falls into the verify-clear branch. Corrupted or hand-edited state produces a clean bill of health instead of a block.

Item 7: the 30s value is not shown to be derived from anything. It is a hardcoded module constant, not tied to the configured max-index-lag window that trigger (e) is defined against. If configured max index lag exceeds 30s, verify-clear can be granted before the Jira index could plausibly have caught up, which is the exact window the gate exists to close. Defensibility is asserted, not demonstrated.

Item 7: clock inconsistency. Audit entries are stamped from lock.state.clock (an injectable clock), but the age comparison uses wall-clock Date.now(). Tests that drive state.clock therefore cannot exercise the 30s threshold under the time source they control.

Item 11 (dry-run documented exit list complete): the documented list (0, 2, 6, 8, 9, 15, 16-19) omits EXIT.CONFIG_INVALID (1), which is reachable on the dry-run path because submit calls resolveCredentials() whenever unresolved search evidence exists and every credential-validation failure exits 1. EXIT.MALFORMED_CONTENT (13) and EXIT.AMBIGUOUS_HISTORY (14) are also plausibly reachable during draft/sidecar load before the dry-run early return, as is EXIT.PREFLIGHT_FAILED (3) if dry-run performs createmeta preflight.

Item 13 (doctor smoke-tests POST /rest/api/3/search/jql including cursor pagination): the excerpt shows only an elided comment, 'searchOnce smoke test (search/jql incl. pagination per its own implementation)'. A single searchOnce call does not demonstrate a nextPageToken cursor round-trip. Not confirmed from supplied evidence.

SKILL.md gate-weakening review (explicitly requested): the packet supplies none of the five diffs. This check could not be performed at all. The passing test run is not evidence about SKILL.md content, since these files govern pipeline behavior and are not executed by the suite.

Test-quality scrutiny (explicitly requested): tests/jira-queue.test.mjs is not included in the packet. A green run of 9 files says nothing about whether network errors, fence races, and lock contention are exercised through real mechanics or stubbed to the point of being unfalsifiable. The one detail supplied (a synchronous-blocking-primitive lint implemented as a source-text regex) is a weak, brittle assertion form and mildly lowers confidence in the rest.

Item 16 partially failed on the operational side: doctor hard-fails with CONFIG_INVALID when myself.emailAddress !== credentials.email, but Jira Cloud omits emailAddress for accounts whose email visibility is not public or when the token lacks the required scope. In that common case emailAddress is undefined and a correctly configured tenant fails doctor outright. The comparison is also raw and case-sensitive with no normalization.

securityFindings.summary: verify-clear NaN fail-open. A marker with an unparseable or missing `at` timestamp makes the age comparison NaN, which evaluates false against the 30s threshold and grants verify-clear. The duplicate-prevention gate opens precisely under the corrupted-state conditions it is meant to defend. Fix: reject non-finite parsed timestamps as inconclusive (treat as age 0) rather than letting them fall through.

The /myself identity assertion is detection-after-transmission, not prevention, and it runs only in doctor. By the time /rest/api/3/myself is called, the API token has already been sent to whatever host siteUrl names. submit and the other network paths are not shown to perform the assertion. The help text calling /myself 'the trust check' therefore repeats, in weaker form, the overstatement that checklist item 16 was written to eliminate: the *.atlassian.net rule is not an exfiltration boundary, and neither is a post-hoc doctor-only check.

Credential-content disclosure path not closed in the shown code. Only validateCredentialFilePath is shown wrapping an error in sanitize(); the credential read path is elided as 'UTF-8 decode + JSON.parse + exact key check, all fail() on error'. Modern V8 JSON.parse errors embed surrounding source text from the parsed string, so an unsanitized JSON error from a malformed credential file can echo token bytes into stderr and logs. Checklist item 19 cannot be marked resolved without seeing sanitize() applied on that path.

Credential file checks cover the file (uid, mode 0o077, dev/ino revalidation, O_NOFOLLOW) but not its containing directory. A group- or world-writable parent directory still permits unlink-and-replace by another local user; the uid check limits impersonation but does not eliminate denial or substitution with an attacker-chosen file the attacker then chowns via a directory they control.

fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW || 0 silently degrades to no flag on platforms lacking it. The dev/ino comparison against the lstat result does catch a symlink substitution (link inode vs target inode differ), so the control degrades safely, but the degradation is implicit and undocumented; an operator on such a platform is not told the primary defense is absent and only the secondary check remains.

Node reserves exit codes in the 1-13 range for its own failures (1 uncaught fatal exception, 9 invalid argument, 13 unsettled top-level await, among others). EXIT.CONFIG_INVALID=1, APPROVAL_EXPIRED=9 and MALFORMED_CONTENT=13 collide with those, so a crash inside the tool is indistinguishable to a caller from a defined semantic outcome. The internal inventory is collision-free as item 10 requires, but any automation branching on these codes can misread a crash as a business result.

materialDissent: Deviation 2 (VERIFY_CLEAR_MIN_AGE_MS = 30000) is the one deviation I do not accept as non-material. It is a duplicate-safety window chosen with no stated derivation, hardcoded rather than configurable, and not reconciled with the configured max-index-lag concept that trigger (e) already depends on. A magic constant that decides when it is safe to POST again belongs in config with an explicit relationship to the index-lag bound, and the choice warranted a check-back rather than an implementer call.

I dissent from treating the QC gate as complete on the evidence supplied. Two of the packet's own explicit review instructions (the five SKILL.md diffs, the 625-line test file) shipped with no artifact attached, and the approved spec's 'Known issues for implementation' section is present only as a 19-item paraphrase. Verifying an implementation against a restatement of the checklist rather than the checklist itself is not an independent verification, and item 14 in particular ('confirm this doesn't contradict the spec text you have access to') is unanswerable because that spec text was not provided.

I do not agree that the /myself assertion discharges SEC-R17-1/SEC-R17-2. It changes the overstatement rather than removing it. The honest framing is: nothing in this design prevents credential transmission to a wrong host; doctor detects it afterward, and only if doctor is run.
review.strongestObjection: The duplicate-prevention gate, which is the entire security and correctness rationale for this subsystem, fails open on malformed input. In preMutationDuplicateGate, `youngestMarkerAge` is computed as `Date.now() - Math.max(...markers.map(e => Date.parse(e.at)))`. Any marker whose `at` field is missing, truncated, or non-ISO makes that expression NaN; `NaN < VERIFY_CLEAR_MIN_AGE_MS` is false; control falls to the `verify-clear` branch and the draft is cleared for POST. The gate is strongest against well-formed state and weakest against corrupted state, which inverts the threat model. The suite passes, which means no test feeds a malformed timestamp into this path -- and that is itself the more troubling signal, because a 625-line test file that covers 'marker closure' and 'all submitting-sidecar shapes' should have hit it. One line (reject non-finite parses as age zero) fixes the defect; the missing test is the larger question about how much the green run actually certifies.
unresolvedQuestions: Where are the five SKILL.md diffs? Without them the requested gate-weakening review is impossible, and these files govern pipeline authority checks rather than mere documentation.

Where is tests/jira-queue.test.mjs? Specifically: are network errors injected at the fetch boundary or above it; are fence races driven by real concurrent lock acquisition or by hand-set fence tokens; does any test feed a malformed marker timestamp into the verify-clear path?

Does the fetch-error classifier read error.cause.code? Under undici, a connection failure surfaces as `TypeError: fetch failed` with the ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED code on `.cause`, not on the top-level error. If the classifier inspects error.code, PRE_CONNECTION_CODES never matches and everything degrades to `unknown`. That direction is fail-safe, so the tests would still pass while the allowlist is dead code -- item 9 would be satisfied by accident, not by design.

Does doctor tolerate a Jira Cloud account whose emailAddress is withheld for privacy? As written, `myself.emailAddress !== credentials.email` hard-fails on undefined, which will break doctor for legitimate tenants.
Is the 30s window related to the configured max index lag that trigger (e) is defined against, or independent of it? If independent, what happens when configured lag exceeds 30s?
Does CONFIG.md state the maxAttempts semantics, or only the CLI help text? An operator sets maxAttempts in config, so the definition must live where the value is set.

Deviation 4: when a discarded draft resolves audit-only against late direct evidence, does `status` (or any operator-facing surface) show that a discarded draft corresponds to a real Jira key, or is that association reachable only by reading the audit trail?

Does `unavailable: true` from the duplicate gate reach the operator distinguishably? It currently maps to EXIT.STATE_ERROR (2), identical to 'submit requires approved state', so 'retry in 30 seconds' and 'permanent state violation' are indistinguishable to automation.
Do the block messages actually direct the operator to `resolve`, as item 1 requires? The shown strings say 'until duplicate evidence is resolved' without naming the command.
review.recommendation:
Decision: REVISE. Real defects exist, none redesign-level, so this is not a block; but too much of the mandatory checklist is unverifiable from the packet for an approve.

Per-item verdicts (C = confirmed, P = partial, F = failed, U = unverifiable from supplied evidence):

1 P -- submitDraft gates on unresolvedDuplicateEntries/unresolvedDirectEvidence and exits 6; the predicates defining "unretired" are not shown, and the messages do not name the `resolve` command.
2 U -- recovery path not excerpted. ATTEMPT_OUTCOMES containing 'aborted-before-post' is necessary but not sufficient.
3 C (as defined) -- present in ATTEMPT_OUTCOMES and distinct from 'failed'; that the validator consumes this set is implied, not shown.
4 U -- deviation 4's description is consistent with the requirement; no code shown.
5 U -- unresolvedRetryVerify gating exists in submit, but I cannot tie it to trigger (e) or confirm status surfacing.
6 C -- clearFreeze nulls all four fields. Only caveat: null rather than delete, which matters if any validator distinguishes absent from null.
7 F -- see failedChecks and QC-SEC-1. Note the requirement's "every retired marker" is correctly implemented via Math.max (newest marker), so that part is right; the NaN path, the underived constant, and the Date.now()/state.clock split are the failures.
8 C -- doctor emits both the has-scheme and cannot-determine warnings and the CLI text states necessary-but-not-sufficient.
9 P -- the allowlist is conservative and correctly excludes the ambiguous mid-flight codes (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE), so no over-match into 'failed'. TLS entries are defensible: those failures precede request-byte transmission. The extraction plumbing is unverified (see unresolvedQuestions).
10 C internally -- 0,1,2,3,6,8,9,13,14,15,16,17,18,19 are distinct; 10-12 absent. External collision with Node's reserved codes flagged as QC-SEC-6.
11 F -- documented list incomplete.
12 U -- documented in help; no code shown.
13 U -- pagination not demonstrated.
14 P -- CLI help is unambiguous; the spec text was not supplied, so the contradiction check requested is unanswerable. CONFIG.md wording unverified.
15 Non-material and correct in direction -- reconcile-from-unknown forces verification before resubmit, matching item 2's posture. Implementer's call was right and did not need interrogation. Code unverified.
16 P -- assertion present, but post-transmission, doctor-only, and likely to hard-fail on privacy-restricted Jira Cloud accounts.
17 C -- this is the best-executed item in the packet: realpath plus lstat, O_NOFOLLOW open, dev/ino revalidation against the lstat, uid and mode checks, handle closed in finally. Residual gaps are QC-SEC-4/5.
18 P -- findCredentialSymlinks is invoked and warns; scope (which roots, symlink vs hardlink) unverified.
19 P -- sanitize() imported and used at one shown site; the credential-parse error path is elided (QC-SEC-3).

Deviations: 1 non-material (fail-safe direction -- fewer POSTs than a retries-after-first reading -- but must be stated in CONFIG.md, not only CLI help). 2 MATERIAL, see materialDissent. 3 non-material. 4 non-material and correct; the open question is operator surfacing, not the semantics.

To clear this gate:
1. Fix the NaN fail-open (treat non-finite parses as age zero) and add a test that feeds a malformed marker timestamp.
2. Either derive 30s from the configured max-index-lag bound or make it configurable with a documented floor; use the injected clock, not Date.now().
3. Complete the dry-run exit list (add 1, and 3/13/14 if reachable), or add a test that asserts the documented set equals the reachable set.
4. Make doctor tolerate a withheld emailAddress -- warn and fall back to accountId rather than hard-failing -- and normalize case on comparison.
5. Confirm sanitize() wraps the credential-parse error path.
6. Give the transient "markers younger than 30s" case a distinguishable signal from a permanent state violation.
7. Supply the five SKILL.md diffs, tests/jira-queue.test.mjs, and the spec's verbatim Known-issues section, then re-run this gate on items 2, 4, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15 plus the pipeline-integration review -- those seven items and the SKILL.md check are currently unaudited, not passed.

The 52 confidence reflects roughly half the checklist resting on assertion rather than evidence; the code that I could see is generally careful, and item 17 in particular is well done.
